A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same attention-based concept-erasure work, despite the change from EIUP to GIE and substantial extensions. The text, equations, tables and figures support comparison. v1 has no appendix; v2 includes readable Appendices A–I.

before.justification: v1 reports original I2P nudity-erasure, Ring-A-Bell red-teaming, style-erasure and multi-concept experiments, plus COCO-30K FID and CLIP results.

after.justification: v2 reports original NSFW, style and object-erasure results, with additional adapter, prompt-length, multi-concept and diffusion-backbone evaluations in its appendices.

M1.justification: v1 uses manually selected suppression weights, including -10 for nudity and -0.5 for style. v2 adds an MLP adapter trained on GPT-4o-selected scales to predict suppression from initial cross-attention statistics. Section 4.3 also adds semantic-distance filtering of overlapping target concepts before multi-concept injection. These change the procedure beyond renaming EIUP as GIE.

E1.justification: v2 retains I2P, COCO-30K, NSFW and style erasure, but adds common-object erasure with exact terms and synonyms, Hokusai alongside Monet and van Gogh, and a BLIP-2-captioned NSFW prompt dataset. It also tests larger target combinations and absent targets. The Ring-A-Bell adversarial-prompt evaluation in v1 is removed.

E2.justification: The I2P and COCO comparisons add SD v2.1, SD + NEG, Safe-CLIP, ESD-x and SPM alongside the retained SLD and ESD-u comparators. COCO Table 1 also removes the SD v1.4 entry present in v1, although SD v1.4 remains the reference model elsewhere.

E3.justification: New protocols include 100 images per object prompt with CLIP classification, three 2,000-prompt length groups, and a 200-image joint-erasure evaluation. v2 adds SD v1.5, v2.1 and XL deployments and reports Realistic Vision v6.0 for Figures 5–8, whereas v1 states all experiments use SD v1.4. ESD-u is described as non-cross-attention fine-tuning instead of cross-attention fine-tuning; this establishes a reported configuration revision, not that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds quantitative adapter-versus-fixed-scale ablations, an embedding-permutation example, prompt-length sensitivity tests, non-target preservation checks and cross-backbone analyses. The injection-position analysis now includes a random position and reports little positional effect, replacing v1's preference based on image damage after [SOT]. The attack-based Ring-A-Bell robustness analysis is removed.

E5.justification: v1 explicitly states that I2P images use the dataset's supplied prompt–seed pairs; v2 omits this evaluation seed information. Neither version reports confidence intervals, error bars, significance tests or repeated-run variability. The additional generated-image counts in v2 are sample-size information, not evidence of uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes substantially: v1 reports EIUP FID 13.30, best among its comparators; v2 reports GIE FID 15.452, with SPM best at 13.566 and GIE highest in CLIP score at 26.433. The I2P reference total changes from 1,434 to 1,037. These are revised results, not an established controlled performance change. v2 adds object, adapter, prompt-length and backbone results and removes red-teaming results. Table 2 reports target-object removal rates of 0.92–1.00, but also non-target rates up to 0.15.

T1.justification: v2 adds mathematical definitions for the layerwise attention-statistic vector, adapter regression objective and semantic-distance filtering rule in Equations 9–11. Much of the original attention construction is retained or reformulated. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs; Appendix A offers qualitative reasoning supported by an example.

C1.justification: The central contribution changes from a wholly training-free erasure method to a method that trains an adapter while avoiding diffusion-model fine-tuning. v2 introduces adaptive suppression and generalization to unseen concepts as contributions and broadens the headline scope to common objects. The earlier conclusion's explicit red-teaming robustness claim is removed.

C2.justification: v2 explains adaptive suppression as balancing erasure against semantic damage and attributes unseen-concept transfer to learning a shared suppression standard. It adds overlapping-concept interference as a failure mechanism. Appendix B replaces v1's semantic-coherence rationale for injection position with a claim of little positional effect. v1's stated limitations involving side nudity and male upper bodies are omitted.

D1.justification: v2 adds algorithm pseudocode and a code/data link. Appendix D specifies the adapter's 16–64–32–1 architecture, 60-prompt labeling procedure, suppression search range, Adam optimizer, 0.001 learning rate, 2,000 epochs and estimated labeling/training costs. It also documents caption construction and CLIP classification. Conversely, v1's explicit 50 diffusion steps and guidance scale of 7.5 are no longer specified.

R1.justification: v2 substantially refocuses the literature discussion toward text-encoder fine-tuning, diffusion-module fine-tuning, pluggable adapters and inference intervention. It adds substantive discussion of Safe-CLIP, SPM and several prompt-refinement methods, while removing much of the LLM detoxification and red-teaming discussion. v1's explicit claim to be the first attention-map manipulation approach is replaced by positioning around growth inhibitors and adaptive suppression.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and method narrative are extensively rewritten around GIE and growth-inhibitor terminology. Related Work and Background become separate sections, experiments are consolidated into setup/results sections, and analyses and implementation information are organized into Appendices A–I. The title, author information and conference framing also change.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column ACM layout to a single-column ICLR layout. The method diagram is redrawn to include the adapter, attention visualizations gain synonym examples, the main NSFW chart becomes a multi-panel comparison, and Table 1 is transposed and expanded. Numerous analysis displays are added, while the elicitation schematic and red-teaming chart disappear. Some style and multi-concept examples are retained or rearranged.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for the method's erasure–preservation tradeoff through the adapter ablation in Appendix C, Figure 11 and Table 3, broader relevant comparisons, and concrete training details in Appendix D. These address important weaknesses in v1's manual-scale selection and narrow comparative evidence. The gains are qualified by the loss of adversarial testing and new reporting inconsistencies: the ORR definition conflicts with its interpretation, and Table 2 contradicts the claimed non-target maximum of 0.05. Despite these weaknesses, the methodological justification and reproducibility information improve substantially.
